open_points.subject: agent-authority withdrawal without a project id
open_points.text: A10 says an operation on a project that names none uses the session's active project; A08 says a withdrawal names the pointer only and uses the pointer's own project.
open_points.question: For a Kernel withdrawal, is authorization checked against the pointer's project regardless of the active project, or is the active project used because the request names no project?
options: Use the pointer's own project
Use the active project
Require the pointer's project also to be active
open_points.default_guess: Use the pointer's own project, treating A08 as the operation-specific rule.

open_points.subject: agent-authority calls racing access changes
open_points.text: A10 says a call whose transaction commits before a session change is accepted and one that commits after is rechecked, but read calls do not necessarily commit a transaction.
open_points.question: At what event is an agent-authority read ordered against revocation, archiving or session end?
options: At transaction or snapshot start
At completion of authorization checks
At answer commit or dispatch
Recheck immediately before returning the answer
open_points.default_guess: Run the authorization check and read in one serializable transaction, ordered at that transaction's snapshot or commit point.

open_points.subject: reuse of an ended agent-session identity
open_points.text: A11 removes every record of an ended session, relies on Kernel never reusing its identity, yet says registration of an ended identity creates a new session while old audit entries keep naming the same identity.
open_points.question: How can Registry preserve the claim that audit entries naming a session identity mean one session if that identity is registered again?
options: Keep a durable tombstone and refuse reuse
Accept reuse and add an incarnation identity
Accept reuse and allow audit ambiguity
open_points.default_guess: Keep a durable tombstone and refuse registration of an ended identity.

open_points.subject: access version on Kernel session end
open_points.text: A12 says ending a session states the current version, while its next rule specifically lists ending among the owner's version-checked actions; A11 also lets Kernel end a session.
open_points.question: Must Cabinet Kernel's 'end an agent session' state and match the access version, or is the version required only when the owner ends it?
options: Both Kernel and owner must state it
Only the owner must state it
Neither must state it
open_points.default_guess: Require it only for the owner, because Kernel owns the underlying agent-session lifecycle.

open_points.subject: owner-session, CSRF and confirmation values
open_points.text: A13 calls the session protected and uses bearer, CSRF and one-time confirmation values, but neither A13 nor M11 requires these values to be unpredictable, confidential in diagnostics and logs, or resistant to guessing.
open_points.question: What entropy, generation and non-disclosure rules apply to the owner-session cookie value, CSRF value and pending confirmation value?
options: Cryptographically random bearer values with a specified minimum entropy and no logging
UUID-format values under the existing identity rule
Deterministic signed values
open_points.default_guess: Use cryptographically random values with at least 256 bits of entropy, compare them safely and never log or disclose them.

open_points.subject: owner-session cookie transport
open_points.text: A13 says the cookie is sent only over HTTPS when the interface is reached from another machine, without saying whether the same cookie may be sent over HTTP when Registry is reached locally.
open_points.question: Is the owner-session cookie always Secure, or may a local HTTP owner interface receive it?
options: Always require HTTPS and set Secure
Allow local HTTP with a non-Secure cookie
Use distinct local and remote cookie policies
open_points.default_guess: Always require HTTPS and set the cookie Secure.

open_points.subject: failed confirmation submission
open_points.text: A13 says the pending confirmation is used up after session and CSRF checks whatever the answer, including a value bound to another action, but does not distinguish a submitted stale or random value from the session's actual pending value.
open_points.question: After valid session and CSRF checks, does any confirmation submission consume the session's pending value, or only submission of that exact pending value?
options: Any submission consumes the pending value
Only the exact pending value consumes it
An exact but expired or wrongly bound value consumes it; an unrelated value does not
open_points.default_guess: Only the exact pending value consumes it, including when it is expired or bound to different inputs.

open_points.subject: removed artifact types in the agent projection
open_points.text: A22 says every pointer of a removed type remains and that the agent projection still carries them, while State 1 defines the agent projection as carrying only current published pointers, without superseded or withdrawn history.
open_points.question: Which pointers of a removed type appear in the agent projection?
options: Only its published pointer, if any
Every pointer of the removed type
No pointer of a type no longer declared
open_points.default_guess: Only the published pointer, preserving the State 1 projection rule.

open_points.subject: display names in the import mapping
open_points.text: A16 says the mapping shows the display name each picked project will arrive under, but does not say whether it must be newly supplied by the owner, may default to the imported name, or when confirmation is refused for its absence.
open_points.question: For each picked project, what determines its imported display name and is an explicit replacement name mandatory?
options: The owner must provide a new nonblank display name
Use the source name unless the owner replaces it
Require a new name only when the source name violates the naming rule
open_points.default_guess: Require the owner to provide a new nonblank display name for every picked project.

open_points.subject: valid imported artifact history
open_points.text: A16 rejects more than one published pointer and certain superseded ordering, but permits histories with no published pointer, a published non-highest version, or a highest superseded pointer, although imported pointers cannot be withdrawn and publication leaves exactly the newest version published.
open_points.question: What exact status pattern must imported versions 1..n have?
options: Versions 1..n-1 must be superseded and version n published
Any sequence with at most one published pointer is valid
Histories with no published pointer are also valid
open_points.default_guess: Require versions 1 through n-1 to be superseded and version n to be published.

open_points.subject: two concurrent import confirmations
open_points.text: A16 rechecks at confirmation and stores the import and unique migration closure in one transaction, but does not state how two confirmations that both begin while no closure exists are ordered or what happens to the loser.
open_points.question: What is the required outcome when two valid import confirmations race?
options: Serialize them: one succeeds and the other is refused because the closure exists
Refuse both
Let a storage uniqueness error determine the result
open_points.default_guess: Serialize them so exactly one commits and the other receives the normal already-closed refusal.

open_points.subject: replacement of the uploaded import file
open_points.text: M11 says the next upload replaces the session's uploaded file, while A16 says unreadable, malformed or oversized files are refused without saying whether such an attempted upload has already replaced a previously valid file.
open_points.question: Does a refused upload discard and replace the valid file already held in the owner session?
options: Replace only after the new file passes upload-level parsing and size checks
Every attempted upload immediately replaces it
A refused upload clears the old file but keeps no new one
open_points.default_guess: Replace the old file only after the new upload passes size and basic format checks.

open_points.subject: configuration secret length
open_points.text: A17 requires each secret to be at least 32 bytes long but does not define whether configuration supplies raw bytes, encoded text, or decoded secret material.
open_points.question: Against which representation is the 32-byte minimum measured, and which encodings are accepted?
options: Decoded raw secret bytes
UTF-8 bytes of the configured text
A fixed encoding such as base64 whose decoded value is measured
open_points.default_guess: Require canonical base64 and measure at least 32 decoded bytes.

open_points.subject: backup encryption
open_points.text: A18 requires every backup to be encrypted with the backup key but specifies no authenticated-encryption scheme, nonce handling, key derivation, format authentication or algorithm/version marker.
open_points.question: What exact cryptographic backup format makes encryption, tamper detection and later decryption verifiable?
options: Specify an authenticated-encryption format and algorithm
Use storage-level encryption only
Leave the cipher and format to each implementation
open_points.default_guess: Define a versioned authenticated-encryption format using a modern AEAD with a fresh nonce per backup.

open_points.subject: restoring a backup made with an old key
open_points.text: A18 says old backups remain encrypted with their old keys and the owner keeps those keys, while A17 configures exactly one backup key and no rule says how a restore selects or supplies an old key.
open_points.question: How is the key for an older backup provided and verified during restore?
options: A host restore tool explicitly receives the archived key
Registry configuration supports a key ring
Old backups cannot be restored after key rotation
open_points.default_guess: Use a host-side restore tool that explicitly receives the archived key from the owner's vault.

open_points.subject: restore after the one-time migration
open_points.text: A18 permits restoring any retained backup and only requires replaying later erasures, restrictions and relationship ends; restoring a backup from before the successful import removes the migration closure that A16 and R0-79 rely on to forbid a second import.
open_points.question: May production restore a backup predating the successful migration, and if so how is the permanent one-import closure restored?
options: Forbid restoring a pre-migration backup after migration succeeds
Keep the migration closure outside the restored store
Require the owner to recreate the closure without reimporting
Allow another import
open_points.default_guess: Forbid use of a pre-migration backup once the migration has succeeded.

open_points.subject: backup and running-release compatibility
open_points.text: A18 verifies a backup against the release that made it, but says production may later replace its store with that backup; A17 refuses to start when the store version differs from the running release.
open_points.question: Which release must perform a restore, and how is an older backup migrated to the current store version?
options: Restore with its recorded release, then run the normal release migration
Only backups matching the current release may be restored
The restore tool migrates the backup directly
open_points.default_guess: Restore with the recorded release and then apply the normal verified release-upgrade procedure.

open_points.subject: security-review catalogue
open_points.text: A21 declares the review complete against nine categories whose questions are defined only in `skills/spec-authoring/SECURITY_REVIEW_EVIDENCE.md`, but those questions are not present in the accepted texts.
open_points.question: What exact questions and completion criteria define each security-review category for agents working from these texts alone?
options: Include the catalogue and its questions in the accepted text
Make the referenced document a versioned normative input
Treat the category names alone as sufficient
open_points.default_guess: Copy the nine categories' questions and completion criteria into the accepted State 2 text.
